explanations.7: The command runs git worktree list, and if it fails (because we're not in a git repo), the || operator triggers the error handler in curly braces instead of crashing.
explanations.16: The {1} is a placeholder that fzf replaces with the first field (the path) from each line, so the preview shows what files are in each worktree directory.
explanations.19: We use awk to extract just the first column (the directory path) from the selected line, since fzf returns the whole line but we only need the path part.
explanations.23: This creates a new directory path by taking the git repo root and appending the branch name (with slashes converted to dashes) so worktrees don't conflict with each other.
